scope: Own400 checkpoint, two previously selected cases, eight temporal video frames per arm; reviewed before R12A scores. Not a full-suite quality estimate.

VP004.R1: Scene remains clear, held thin material deforms/partly disappears late; no convincing requested propagating fracture.
VP004.R10A: Scene clear, held material largely remains static with small late variations; no convincing fracture.
VP004.R12A: Scene clear and material/people persist; mostly static with small material changes. No visible successful bend-until-crack propagation in sampled frames. No demonstrated repair of this process.

VP010.R1: Mop moves but head/water develop implausible loop-like forms late.
VP010.R10A: Mop largely static; no clear requested mopping progression.
VP010.R12A: Mop moves from rear/center toward foreground while recognizable head/shaft persist. More task movement than R10A, but water develops abnormal raised white splash/foam and broad smooth patches; not convincing contact-dependent absorption or a clean physically correct output.

decision: Partial evidence that R12A restores requested movement in VP010 and avoids the severe global texture seen in R11B examples; full PC/SA/Joint and state-read/order controls still required. Do not count motion alone as physical success or these2cases as global improvement.
